forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Unchanged at 21%. Four days since last forecast; no resolution-triggering AGI announcement. Sequoia's 'AGI is here, now' essay (late May) frames long-horizon agents as 'functionally AGI' — opinion piece, not the lab-declaration-or-3-researcher attestation the resolution criterion requires. Dario Amodei's Davos 2026 'AGI within a few years (2027)' restatement and Hassabis's 'foothills of the singularity' language remain forward-looking rather than declarative. OpenAI's $24B Q1 ARR and Anthropic's $30B → $43-45B trajectory confirm extraordinary commercial traction without a YES-triggering event. 31 months to deadline; time-decay continues to dominate without a positive shock.
forecasts.base_rate: Major paradigm-defining technology claims with sub-3-year horizons resolve YES <20% historically. AI Impacts 2023 survey median for HLMI clusters 2040-2047. Metaculus community ~25% by 2027, ~50% by 2031. Kalshi contributors ~40% on OpenAI AGI by 2030, but this question's resolution (public lab announcement OR 3+ leading researchers) is stricter than market questions on a single firm.

factors_up.factor: Continued frontier capability scaling (Gemini 3.5 Flash, Claude Mythos Preview clears 32-step cyber range, GPT-5.5 derivatives)
Amodei (Davos 2026): AGI 'within a few years (2027)' — insider conviction signal
Anthropic + SpaceX/xAI Colossus 1 compute deal accelerates training compute access

factors_down.factor: OpenAI/MS contract previously stripped 'AGI' clause — deprecates term for high-stakes resolution
No researcher consensus near the 3+ attestation threshold; public discourse still framed as 'approaching' not 'achieved'
Time decay: 31 months to deadline, no announcement, no clear bridge to one
Jensen Huang's 'we've achieved AGI' (March 2026) was not picked up as a resolution event — demonstrates the ambiguity bar

key_uncertainties: Whether a single lab CEO declaration plus carefully-coordinated researcher statements could resolve YES in 2027-2029
Pace of agentic capability gains — could a clear human-equivalent-economist agent shift discourse?
Whether 'AGI' remains the preferred public framing or is replaced by capability gates
update_triggers: Public AGI declaration by an OpenAI/Anthropic/DeepMind/xAI principal
3+ leading AI researchers (e.g., LeCun, Hinton, Bengio, Hassabis, Sutskever) jointly attesting AGI
Major frontier model release demonstrating clear human-level generalisation across novel domains
Policy/regulatory action defining AGI in a binding way

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Unchanged at 25%. Fast Company, Inc and Quartz coverage of McKinsey's 200 tech/support cuts (late 2025) plus Sternfels's signal of further non-client reductions reinforces the trajectory rather than accelerating it. BCG is still growing headcount, but tilted toward AI/tech specialists vs. generalists — consistent with re-mix rather than collapse. McKinsey's Lilli running 500k+ prompts/month internally with consultants reporting up to 30% time-savings is now the dominant productivity-substitution story. ~25% of entry-level consulting/finance postings require AI fluency vs <5% two years ago. None of this yet maps to a ≥33% headline decline in revenue or employment vs 2024 baseline — but the directional pressure is increasingly hard to ignore.
forecasts.base_rate: Major professional-services revenue declines of ≥33% in 5 years are rare (post-2008 banking; legal services after 2010 LPO wave was -10-15%). AI-driven displacement in white-collar professional services is a novel reference class with limited base data.

factors_up.factor: McKinsey ongoing 10% workforce cut plus visible non-client reductions; Bain/Deloitte/KPMG/Accenture all cutting
AI fee compression pressure visible in client renegotiations (TheStreet coverage)
Entry-level pyramid model under structural pressure: 25% of postings now require AI fluency
DeployCo ($4B OpenAI consulting subsidiary, May 2026) signals direct LLM-to-client substitution emerging

factors_down.factor: BCG continues to grow — sector heterogeneity; AI fluency repricing, not contraction
5-year horizon allows firms to reposition revenue toward AI implementation services (often pricier per-engagement)
Attribution barrier: ≥33% decline 'primarily attributed to AI' by 2+ credible analyses is a high resolution bar
Underlying demand for advisory remains strong; consulting often counter-cyclical in restructuring phases

key_uncertainties: Whether sector revenue holds via AI-implementation pricing while headcount falls sharply
Whether 'economic consultancy' resolution scope is interpreted strictly (MBB+Big Four advisory) or broadly
How analysts will attribute declines (AI vs. cyclical) by end-2030
update_triggers: MBB or Big Four reporting -15%+ revenue YoY
Industry-wide headcount data showing ≥15% YoY contraction
Major credible analyses (FT, McKinsey Global Institute, Oxford-style studies) attributing decline to AI

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: Unchanged at 2%. Ipsos (14-20 May) confirms Reform 27%, Labour 20% — a sustained 7pp Reform lead. PollCheck moving average puts Reform 27.3% vs Labour 19.7%. Labour now firmly in the high-teens to low-twenties, with Greens (13-15%) and LD (13-14%) crowding the centre-left. The Andy Burnham leadership challenge speculation (Makerfield by-election context) is a minor signal but not enough to shift trajectory absent a Labour bounce. Up to 3-4 years to the next GE provides ample time for swing — but Labour would need a 7-9pp swing while Reform consolidates, and the historical base rate for governing-party recoveries of this magnitude from this position is low.
forecasts.base_rate: Mid-term polling deficits of ~7-10pp in UK politics recovered ~25% of the time pre-2010. Post-2015 polling has been more volatile; Reform's right-wing populist insurgency is more analogous to BNP/UKIP late 2010s plus Trump-era Republican consolidation. Governing parties trailing by >5pp ~2 years out lose the next GE ~70-80% of the time.

factors_up.factor: Up to 3-4 years until next GE allows for cyclical recovery and event shocks
Reform support partly populist — could compress under genuine campaign scrutiny

factors_down.factor: Sustained ~7-9pp deficit across all major pollsters
Crowded left-of-centre vote (Lab + Greens + LD) splits potential Labour pickup
Burnham leadership speculation suggests internal instability; rarely a winning electoral signal
Reform building infrastructure (candidates, ground operation) at scale — late entrants typically underperform; Reform now mature

key_uncertainties: Whether Labour replaces Starmer and how a new leader polls
Reform's ability to survive sustained scrutiny on candidates, policy detail, and finances
Coalition arithmetic if no party wins outright — 'largest party' is achievable on as little as ~22-25% in a fragmented field
update_triggers: Labour pulling level or ahead in any major pollster for 2+ consecutive polls
Reform falling below 22% across multiple pollsters
Major Labour leadership change
Critical incident (economic crisis, government scandal) that resets polling

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: Unchanged at 78%. The 2035 deadline gives ~8.5 more years of compounding capability — a regime in which today's signals (Amodei: AGI ~2027; Hassabis: 'foothills'; Sequoia: 'AGI is here'; Clark: 60% recursive-self-improvement by 2028) compound rather than fade. Anthropic at $43-45B ARR by Q2 2026 and OpenAI at $24B confirm commercial flywheel adequate to fund continued frontier scaling for the rest of the decade. Even with the 'AGI' term being deprecated in commercial contracts, by 2035 the most likely modal outcome is a public consensus-event triggered by either capability demonstration (e.g., autonomous AI economist, AI scientist) or coordinated researcher statement. Stable estimate around 78% reflects high confidence in capability arrival within window, tempered by definitional and political-coordination risk on the resolution event itself.
forecasts.base_rate: AI Impacts 2023 community survey median for HLMI: 2047 (50% probability). Metaculus aggregate ~50-55% by 2031, ~75-80% by 2035. Kalshi/Manifold contributors weighted ~70-75% by 2035. Reference-class: paradigm-defining technologies in their fast-scaling phase typically reach 'consensus arrival' within 10-15 years of breakthrough trigger (transformer 2017 → 2032 mid-point).

factors_up.factor: Compounding capability gains across 8.5 years of frontier training
Anthropic/OpenAI/DeepMind/xAI commercial flywheel funding rest-of-decade scaling
Multiple credible CEO timelines clustering 2027-2030
Increasing political/regulatory pressure to define and declare AGI status (could itself force a resolution event)

factors_down.factor: Definitional contestation — 'AGI' may fragment into multiple competing benchmarks, no clean YES
Possible capability plateau if scaling laws weaken in late 2020s
Coordinated researcher statement requires social consensus that may not form

key_uncertainties: Whether AGI is declared explicitly vs. retrospectively recognised after the fact
Whether capability advancement continues monotonically through 2034 or hits architectural ceiling
Whether geopolitical fragmentation produces divergent national AGI declarations
update_triggers: Plateau-suggesting model releases (significant gap vs hype)
Compute or energy supply constraints binding on frontier training
Public AGI declaration by major lab
Major regulatory regime requiring AGI categorisation

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Unchanged at 7%. No fresh PLA escalation in late May 2026 beyond the Balikatan-2026-response posture (AEI 1 and 8 May): Type 055 + 052D + 054A surface group plus Type 903A in Luzon Strait, plus Liaoning carrier transit on 20 April. These remain coercive signalling rather than the kind of pre-mobilisation, logistical-buildup, or political ultimatum that would precede a blockade or invasion. Cross-strait baseline tension remains elevated but recently stable; no major Lai administration provocation, no Beijing political-cycle deadline forcing action. 44 months to deadline — probability builds slowly with calendar.
forecasts.base_rate: Major cross-strait military operations in modern era: 0 (1958 Quemoy crisis last hot incident). Great power initiation of major military action against high-allied partner under nuclear umbrella in the post-1945 era: ~2-5% annualised. CSIS/RAND wargames suggest PRC self-perceived window opens late 2020s but with high downside cost.

factors_up.factor: PLA modernisation trajectory continues; PLAN visible surface group + carrier operations off Taiwan
US-PRC strategic competition acute under current US administration; risk of miscalculation elevated
Xi's stated political deadlines (centenary of PLA 2027) provide notional forcing function

factors_down.factor: Visible cross-strait deterrence: US strengthening Japan/Philippines/Australia posture (Balikatan 2026 included France, Canada)
Economic catastrophic cost of military action — PRC's own modelling reportedly highlights extreme downside
Recent PLA signalling consistent with coercion-short-of-war doctrine, not pre-invasion mobilisation
Routine drills now interpreted as 'normal' by analysts — escalation latency rather than acceleration

key_uncertainties: Whether a Taiwan political event (DPP doctrine shift, US arms package, sovereignty-relevant statement) could trigger PRC overreaction
PRC internal political stability and Xi's domestic constraints
How a Trump-era US response to PRC coercion shapes incentives
update_triggers: PLA mobilisation patterns inconsistent with exercise scripts (extended sortie rates, ammunition pre-positioning, civilian shipping requisition)
Beijing public ultimatum with deadline
Major cross-strait shooting incident
Visible US re-tasking of carrier strike groups or strategic bombers

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Up 1pp to 11%. April 2026 ONS CPI confirmed at 2.8% (down from 3.3% in March), with the moderation driven by the 1 April energy price cap reset (housing/household services from 5.3% to 1.4%). Core CPIH at 2.8%. The April-to-December path now needs ~0.8pp further fall in 8 months. Plausible if (a) further utility-base-effect drift through summer, (b) services inflation eases from current ~3.5-4% range, and (c) wage growth moderates further. Still below 50/50 given core stickiness and likely autumn services CPI seasonality. Marginal uptick reflects April's surprisingly clean print rather than confirmation of sub-2% arrival.
forecasts.base_rate: UK CPI typically reverts to target with lag of 18-30 months from peak; post-2022 peak (Oct 2022, 11.1%) → 1.7% by Sept 2024 (sub-2% achieved). Current cycle peak (Q4 2025, ~3.8%) → sub-2% would imply faster-than-typical disinflation given still-tight services.

factors_up.factor: April energy price cap reset delivered 0.5pp single-month drop
Core CPIH at 2.8% with services trajectory softening
Wage growth deceleration through 2026 reducing services CPI pressure
Base effects from 2025 H2 still favourable through summer/autumn 2026

factors_down.factor: Services inflation still ~3.5-4% — structural rather than cyclical stickiness
Autumn 2026 energy cap reset typically lifts headline 0.2-0.4pp
Sterling-related import cost risk
Only 8 monthly observations remaining — narrow window

key_uncertainties: Whether services CPI breaks below 3% in any single month
Energy cap calculation for October 2026 cap window
Wage settlement trajectory through summer pay rounds
update_triggers: May 2026 CPI print (due 17 June 2026) below 2.5%
Services CPI dropping below 3% in any month
MPC base rate cuts signalling confidence on inflation
Sterling appreciation reducing import inflation

forecasts.question: Will Spider-Man: Brand New Day gross over $1.5B worldwide by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Up 1pp to 98%. Variety and Screen Daily confirm the Brand New Day trailer hit 718.6M views in first 24 hours — the biggest trailer launch ever, surpassing Deadpool & Wolverine (365M) inside 8 hours. Within 4 days the trailer crossed 1.1B views — the first film trailer ever to do so. This is an extraordinary pre-sales indicator: trailer-view-to-opening-weekend correlation has been positive and strengthening since Avengers: Endgame. The reference class (No Way Home $1.92B, Endgame $2.8B, Avatar Way of Water $2.3B) now looks closer to the modal expectation than the upside scenario. 31 July release date holds. The remaining ~2% risk reflects tail outcomes: catastrophic review reception, summer competitive cannibalisation, or theatrical disruption.
forecasts.base_rate: MCU 'event' films with major returning cast and prior $1B+ predecessor: ~85-90% cross $1B; ~60-70% cross $1.5B. Strong trailer reception adds 10-15pp. Holland-led Spider-Man franchise prior peaks: No Way Home $1.92B (2021), Far From Home $1.13B (2019).

factors_up.factor: Record-shattering trailer reception (1.1B views in 4 days, first ever)
Strong returning cast (Holland, Zendaya, Batalon) plus high-profile additions (Bernthal, Ruffalo)
31 July anchor date, 5-month theatrical window before Dec 31 deadline
Prior film No Way Home set franchise high at $1.92B — sets expectation reference

factors_down.factor: Box office tail risk: critical reception failure or franchise fatigue
Competitive summer slate could compress weekly multiplier
Theatrical disruption (strike, pandemic) — low probability but non-zero

key_uncertainties: China release status and timing
Critical reception and audience scores in opening weekend
Whether the 1.1B trailer views translate at typical conversion rates or overperform
update_triggers: Pre-sales tracking data 2-3 weeks before release
Opening weekend box office vs $200M domestic / $400M global benchmark
Tomatometer score below 80%
Any production / release schedule disruption

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Up 1pp to 99%. CNBC (20 May) reports Anthropic on track for $10.9B Q2 revenue, implying ~$43-45B ARR by end of Q2 2026 — confirming the SaaStr/Sacra figures from April. OpenAI ARR confirmed at $24B in April 2026 ($2B/month). Combined run-rate is ~$67-69B today; with monthly growth of $2-3B at Anthropic alone (sales 'more than doubled in a matter of months'), the $70B combined threshold is almost mechanically guaranteed by Q3 2026 well before the 31 December resolution date. Note: ARR accounting dispute remains (OpenAI argues Anthropic's gross figure overstates by ~$8B vs net; Anthropic's net comp ~$22B). Resolution criterion specifies 'most recent credible reporting (Bloomberg, The Information, FT, or company disclosures)' — which has consistently used the headline gross figures. 1pp residual reflects (a) accounting interpretation risk and (b) catastrophic disruption tail.
forecasts.base_rate: Hyperscale enterprise SaaS revenue trajectories of 2-3x YoY at this scale: ~95% continue trajectory absent macro shock or product failure. No comparable precedent for $70B combined ARR at this growth pace.

factors_up.factor: Anthropic Q2 run-rate trajectory implies ~$45B by end-Q2, with continued doubling pace
OpenAI Codex/DeployCo/Frontier launches expanding monetisable surface area
Microsoft, Google Cloud, AWS partner-channel volume sustaining Bedrock/Foundry/Vertex consumption

factors_down.factor: Accounting dispute: if mainstream press shifts to net-basis reporting, Anthropic headline falls ~$8B
OpenAI growth stalled per Q1 2026 reporting on ChatGPT consumer side — though enterprise compensating
Tail risk of major API outage, safety incident, or regulatory action

key_uncertainties: Whether Q4 2026 reporting uses gross or net ARR conventions
Whether either company experiences late-2026 retention shock
Anthropic IPO timing — potential for additional disclosure that affirms figures
update_triggers: Quarterly ARR disclosures in Q3 or Q4 2026
FT/Bloomberg shift to net-basis Anthropic reporting
Major customer churn or regulatory restriction

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: Unchanged at 38%. OBR March 2026 EFO continues to forecast 1.1% headline GDP growth in 2026, 1.6% in 2027, with real GDP per person growing 1.1%/year through 2026-2030. TFP recovery from 0.3% (2026) to 0.8% (2030) is built in but conditional on investment delivering. Aggregate potential output growth 0.1pp lower than November 2025 due to weaker net inward migration offsetting marginally higher investment. The 2030s arithmetic-mean >1.5% requires either (a) demographics-positive surprise (population growth via migration), (b) TFP pickup above OBR baseline, or (c) AI-driven productivity acceleration manifesting in measured productivity by mid-2030s. Each is plausible but not modal; combined probability around the high-thirties.
forecasts.base_rate: UK 10-year average GDP growth rates: 2010s 2.0%, 2000s 1.7%, 1990s 2.3%, 1980s 2.5%, 1970s 2.5%. Post-financial-crisis productivity slowdown has lowered the central tendency to ~1.5-1.7% range. AI-productivity uplift is a wildcard.

factors_up.factor: OBR TFP recovery built into baseline (0.3% → 0.8% by 2030)
AI-driven productivity surprise possible in mid-2030s — most credible upside lever
Demographic upside if net migration averages >300k/year through decade
Capital investment recovery driven by green transition and AI infrastructure

factors_down.factor: OBR central forecast ~1.1-1.6% growth through 2030 — below required 1.5% threshold
Ageing population pressure on labour force participation
Energy transition transition-cost drag in early 2030s
Fiscal consolidation pressure may limit public investment

key_uncertainties: Whether AI productivity gains show up in measured TFP by mid-2030s
Net migration policy trajectory across multiple governments
Whether services-sector productivity catches up with goods-sector AI gains
Energy cost trajectory and net-zero transition pacing
update_triggers: OBR forecasts moving above 1.5% for sustained period
Productivity data showing TFP acceleration
Major fiscal/industrial policy shift
AI productivity uplift visible in ONS data
